question: What is the difference between morbidity and mortality?

options.A: Morbidity is caused by bacteria, while mortality is caused by physical injuries
options.B: Morbidity applies only to children, while mortality applies only to the elderly
options.C: Morbidity refers to illness and disease rates, while mortality refers to death rates
options.D: Morbidity measures hospital expenses, while mortality measures community income

explanation: Morbidity tracks how many people are sick with a condition, whereas mortality tracks how many people die from it. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h4)

question: How can a nurse researcher make sure their conceptual framework stays practical?

options.A: By avoiding any review of previous literature
options.B: By removing all independent variables from the diagram
options.C: By copying a framework from an unrelated medical study
options.D: By making sure every variable matches a data collection tool

explanation: Every single concept in your framework must be something you can actually measure using surveys, patient charts, or direct observation! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why must everyone step back and not touch the patient while the AED is analyzing or shocking?

options.A: Movement can interfere with rhythm analysis or cause accidental shocks
options.B: Rescuers will catch the electrical current and stop breathing
options.C: The physical vibration of standing nearby stops the machine
options.D: The AED machine requires complete silence to function properly

explanation: Safety rule number one during an AED check: clear everybody! Movement tricks the machine's rhythm reader and can even shock the person touching the patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h6)

question: How must controlled substances be stored on a hospital ward?

options.A: In an open metal tray on the main nurses' station desk
options.B: Inside the patient's bedside locker for easy access
options.C: In a double-locked secure cabinet with restricted key access
options.D: Inside the general refrigerator with food items

explanation: Double-locking prevents theft, diversion, and unauthorized access to dangerous drugs. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is the ultimate purpose of collecting and evaluating data in clinical quality improvement?

options.A: To fulfill government paperwork requirements without changing practice
options.B: To justify cutting nurse salaries during budget reviews
options.C: To drive positive changes in patient care and nursing workflows
options.D: To provide material for academic medical journals only

explanation: Data collection only matters if we use what we learn to make patient care safer and nursing work smoother! [learn more](GST319_U4_T5#GST319_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why is receiving feedback from a tertiary center important for a primary care nurse?

options.A: It allows the primary nurse to take over the role of a specialist doctor
options.B: It reduces the workload at the local clinic to zero
options.C: It builds professional confidence and improves ongoing management of the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever needing medication refills again

explanation: Getting feedback closes the loop! It helps primary nurses learn from specialist outcomes and grow more confident in managing similar cases. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)

question: What does 'therapeutic use of self' mean in nursing?

options.A: Using your personality and insights to connect with patients
options.B: Hiding all personal feelings behind a cold professional mask
options.C: Acting as a close personal friend outside of work hours
options.D: Sharing your own personal medical history with every patient

explanation: Spot on! It means using your own communication style and warmth on purpose to build trust and help the patient feel safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: A relative suddenly gets angry and pulls away during a visit. How should you, as a nurse, view this behavior?

options.A: As a sign that the relative wishes to abandon the patient
options.B: As proof that the relative does not care about the patient
options.C: As a normal reaction during the process of anticipatory grief
options.D: As a personal insult directed at the nursing staff

explanation: Don't take it personally! Anger and withdrawal are just natural ways people react when they are struggling to accept an impending, painful loss. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which emotional reaction is very common in patients right after they acquire a physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference and forgetfulness
options.B: Grief, shock, and depression
options.C: Aggressive pursuit of extreme sports
options.D: Immediate acceptance and joy

explanation: Losing bodily function triggers a deep grief process, much like losing a loved one. Shock and depression are very normal initial responses. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h6)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with recurring kidney stones and severe flank pain. Which diagnostic test is most appropriate to visualize the exact location of the stones in the ureters?

options.A: Intravenous pyelogram
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Pulmonary function test
options.D: Echocardiogram

explanation: An IVP uses contrast dye to highlight the urinary tract, making it very effective for spotting kidney stones causing flank pain. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h2)

question: What does it mean when a nurse decides to 'cluster care' during a shift?

options.A: Grouping all patients with the same diagnosis in one bay
options.B: Doing several care tasks during one room visit to save time
options.C: Handing over multiple patients to a colleague all at once
options.D: Writing all patient charts at the very end of the shift

explanation: Spot on! Clustering care is a smart student trick: instead of walking in and out all day, you combine vitals, meds, and repositioning into one smooth bedside visit. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of food production when we look at it from a public health point of view?

options.A: Creating synthetic medications for hospitals
options.B: Maximizing financial profit for food manufacturers
options.C: Transforming raw natural resources into safe, consumable food
options.D: Eliminating all forms of agriculture globally

explanation: At its core, food production is all about turning what we harvest from nature into safe, nourishing meals for everyone. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h1)

question: Why is the community health planning cycle a continuous loop instead of a straight line?

options.A: Nurses must repeat the exact same paperwork every single month
options.B: Evaluation findings feed back into new assessments to improve future care
options.C: Health problems never change once an intervention is finished
options.D: It stops the community from ever joining in on healthcare

explanation: Exactly! Healthcare doesn't stop. What you learn from evaluating a project helps you plan even better care for the next round. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: Why do dietitians recommend high-fiber complex carbs instead of simple sugars for diabetic patients?

options.A: They stimulate the pancreas to grow new beta cells
options.B: They contain zero calories and cannot be converted into fat
options.C: They slow down digestion and prevent rapid blood sugar spikes
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any diabetes medication

explanation: High-fiber carbs take longer to digest, giving a nice, steady release of energy rather than sending blood sugar through the roof. Brilliant nursing logic! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h5)

question: How does expanding mandatory health insurance help solve healthcare financing problems?

options.A: It creates a reliable, pooled fund that reduces financial barriers for patients
options.B: It allows doctors to set their own salaries without government review
options.C: It forces international donors to double their annual monetary grants
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for primary healthcare centers

explanation: Brilliant! Mandatory insurance keeps a steady flow of money coming into hospitals while saving everyday people from sudden, crushing medical bills. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h8)

question: Why does severe liver disease frequently cause fluid retention (edema)?

options.A: The damaged liver cannot synthesize enough albumin to maintain blood osmotic pressure
options.B: The liver stops producing bile needed for digesting complex carbohydrates
options.C: The stomach absorbs too much salt directly into the portal vein
options.D: The kidneys fail to filter out extra water because of liver congestion

explanation: Brilliant! Albumin is made by the liver and acts like a sponge keeping water inside your blood vessels. Without enough albumin, fluid leaks out into the tissues. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle vaccine hesitancy from a caregiver?

options.A: Telling the caregiver that their personal beliefs are completely wrong
options.B: Listening respectfully to concerns and providing clear facts
options.C: Threatening to withhold other basic primary healthcare services
options.D: Ignoring the questions and quickly administering the injection anyway

explanation: You nailed it! Building trust through patience, empathy, and gentle education works way better than arguing or judging. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h8)

question: A student nurse accidentally pricks a finger with a used injection needle. What is the very first thing to do?

options.A: Suck the puncture site vigorously to extract infected blood
options.B: Cover the wound with adhesive plaster and finish the shift
options.C: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow to trap the virus

explanation: Spot on! Immediate washing with soap and running water helps wash away germs right after an exposure. Always remember this rule! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h7)

question: What happens if a nurse squeezes the resuscitation bag too fast during CPR?

options.A: It lowers blood flow back to the heart by increasing chest pressure
options.B: It causes immediate heart muscle damage
options.C: It makes the chest compressions much deeper
options.D: It instantly stops all electrical activity in the brain

explanation: Too much air pressure inside the chest pushes against the blood vessels returning to the heart, reducing overall blood flow. You've got this! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which types of medications most commonly increase the risk of falls in older adults?

options.A: Multivitamins
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Sedatives and antihypertensives
options.D: Vitamin C supplements

explanation: Drugs that cause dizziness, sleepiness, or sudden drops in blood pressure can easily lead to a fall. Always keep an eye on safety! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h4)

question: What is the main job of descriptive statistics in nursing research?

options.A: To summarize and organize raw healthcare data
options.B: To prove a cause-and-effect relationship between drugs
options.C: To predict future disease outbreaks using probability
options.D: To test complex hypotheses with small sample sizes

explanation: You've got this! Descriptive statistics are simply tools to tidy up large piles of data, making it easy for us to see the main picture without getting bogged down in numbers. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h1)

question: What major risk must nurses watch out for when patients take long-term immunosuppressant drugs?

options.A: Rapid and permanent weight loss
options.B: Increased susceptibility to severe opportunistic infections
options.C: Total loss of taste and smell
options.D: Excessively high blood pressure caused by thickened blood

explanation: When we quiet the immune system to stop it from attacking the body, it also struggles to fight off normal germs. Good patient education on hygiene is key here! [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h7)

question: A nurse is finishing a counselling session by booking a follow-up date and inviting the client back if problems arise. Which GATHER step is this?

options.A: Help
options.B: Return
options.C: Ask
options.D: Explain

explanation: The 'Return' step focuses on planning for future visits, follow-up care, and open-door re-evaluations. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: A community health nurse opens a delivery kit and finds a soap bar, a plastic sheet, a cord tie, a razor blade, and a cloth. What is the primary role of the razor blade?

options.A: To open other plastic packaging
options.B: To rupture the amniotic sac
options.C: To clean the mother's skin
options.D: To cut the umbilical cord

explanation: The razor blade serves as the sterile instrument dedicated to cutting the umbilical cord cleanly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: How do bones react when you do regular physical exercise and put mechanical stress on them?

options.A: They become fragile and brittle because osteoclasts destroy the matrix
options.B: They stop all cellular remodeling to conserve mineral reserves
options.C: They become thicker and stronger through increased osteoblast activity
options.D: They convert entirely from compact bone into spongy bone tissue

explanation: Use them and strengthen them! Exercise signals bone-building osteoblasts to lay down more material, making bones tough. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why does the electrical signal take a short pause at the AV node?

options.A: To stop signals from going backward into the lungs
options.B: To slow down the heart rate during sleep
options.C: To give the SA node time to rest
options.D: To let the ventricles fill up completely with blood first

explanation: That tiny pause is super smart design! It ensures the top chambers finish emptying their blood down into the bottom chambers before the bottom chambers squeeze. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: What are the main signs that tell you it's time to grab and use an AED?

options.A: Confusion and slow, deep respirations
options.B: Severe chest pain and high blood pressure
options.C: Unresponsiveness and no normal breathing
options.D: Dizziness, sweating, and a racing pulse

explanation: Spotting cardiac arrest is key: if someone won't wake up and isn't breathing normally, get that AED ready right away! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why should a nurse in a public hospital care about civil service regulations?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from complying with the nursing and midwifery council acts
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass hospital management during emergency procedures
options.C: It grants the nurse the authority to promote other junior staff members
options.D: It helps align clinical practice with administrative compliance and protects professional rights

explanation: Knowing your workplace rules helps you stay on the right side of management while protecting your rights on the job. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h1)

question: Which global organization maintains the International Classification of Diseases (ICD)?

options.A: The American Nurses Association
options.B: The National Institute of Mental Health
options.C: The World Medical Board
options.D: The World Health Organization

explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) publishes the ICD to track health trends and standardize medical diagnoses worldwide. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to getting accurate data on a busy ward?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully automated digital tools
options.B: Incomplete record-keeping in traditional paper registers
options.C: Heavy workloads and severe shortages of nursing personnel
options.D: Fear of punishment among staff when reporting clinical errors

explanation: We wish we had too much tech! In reality, staff shortages, paper logs, and fear of getting in trouble are the real hurdles—not having an overload of digital tools. [learn more](GST319_U1_T1#GST319_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is it so important to physically clean instruments before disinfecting or sterilizing them?

options.A: To wash away dried blood and tissue that shield germs
options.B: To help the metal cool down quickly after use
options.C: To make the metal look shiny and brand new
options.D: To instantly make the instruments completely sterile

explanation: Spot on! If blood or organic matter is left on an instrument, it acts like a shield protecting germs from the disinfectant. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is food microbiology mainly about?

options.A: The chemical composition of synthetic preservatives
options.B: The nutritional breakdown of proteins in the human gut
options.C: Microorganisms that live in, make, or spoil our food
options.D: Methods of farming crops in dry climates

explanation: You've got this! Food microbiology simply looks at how tiny germs and fungi interact with our food—some help make delicious things like yoghurt, while others cause spoilage. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which group benefits the most from attending a sheltered workshop?

options.A: Skilled healthcare professionals returning from sabbatical
options.B: Healthy young adults seeking high-paying corporate careers
options.C: Experienced artisans looking for advanced technical training
options.D: Individuals with chronic psychiatric or intellectual disabilities

explanation: These workshops are specially tailored for people whose health challenges make it difficult to jump straight into standard jobs. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses and planners must set priorities?

options.A: Healthcare resources are always limited
options.B: All health problems cost the exact same amount to treat
options.C: Government policies forbid buying new medical equipment
options.D: Doctors refuse to participate in budgeting meetings

explanation: That's right! Since funds, drugs, and hands are never endless, we have to choose which urgent needs to tackle first. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the key feature of a latent tuberculosis infection?

options.A: The patient has a productive cough and bloody sputum
options.B: The person is asymptomatic and cannot spread the disease
options.C: The bacteria are rapidly multiplying throughout the bloodstream
options.D: Chest X-rays consistently show severe lung cavity destruction

explanation: Latent TB means the germs are sleeping safely inside the body, kept in check by your immune system. The person feels fine and cannot pass it to others. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h2)

question: Why do nurse researchers like using histograms for patient data?

options.A: To replace the need for ethical board approval in clinical trials
options.B: To quickly visualize the distribution and spread of a data set
options.C: To prove a causal relationship between two separate nursing interventions
options.D: To track the exact medical record number of every patient in a study

explanation: Turning raw numbers into a clear picture helps you spot patterns and averages at a glance. Simple and super helpful in research! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a material commonly used during breast ironing?

options.A: Sterilized surgical scalpels
options.B: Hot metal spatulas
options.C: Heavy wooden pestles
options.D: Heated grinding stones

explanation: Surgical tools are not used in this abusive traditional practice; instead, household items like stones and pestles are heated. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in labor notices severe vaginal bleeding but refuses to go to the hospital until her husband returns from a distant trip. What concept does this situation highlight?

options.A: Superior financial planning for hospital delivery costs
options.B: Effective community-based healthcare mobilization
options.C: Lack of maternal autonomy and delayed emergency decision-making
options.D: Excellent adherence to cultural birth preparation guidelines

explanation: Waiting for absent approval during a life-threatening crisis demonstrates a dangerous absence of personal health autonomy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h3)

question: What is the main job of the insufflation system during a sigmoidoscopy?

options.A: To deliver numbing medicine to the colon
options.B: To cool down the light inside the scope
options.C: To suck out liquid stool and blood
options.D: To gently inflate the bowel with air or gas so the doctor can see better

explanation: You got it! Puffing a little air into the bowel opens up the folds of tissue so the doctor gets a clear view. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To lower the financial cost of operating public hospitals
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To develop knowledge for nursing practice and improve patient outcomes
options.D: To replace physicians in diagnosing complex medical conditions

explanation: Nursing research focuses on building a scientific base for nursing care so patients receive the safest and most effective interventions. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which glands release lubricating fluid near the vaginal opening during sexual arousal?

options.A: Pituitary gland
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Bartholin gland
options.D: Adrenal gland

explanation: Spot on! The Bartholin glands (or greater vestibular glands) help provide natural lubrication. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T3#GNS121_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the defining trait of "vulnerable populations" in community health?

options.A: They experience disproportionate health risks due to disadvantages
options.B: They always have direct access to private health insurance
options.C: They live exclusively in affluent urban neighborhoods
options.D: They hold leadership positions in local government

explanation: Spot on. These are groups who face extra health hurdles because of social, economic, or political disadvantages. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h6)

question: When should you tie up and replace a medical waste bag?

options.A: Completely packed to the brim
options.B: One-quarter full
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: Whenever it starts to smell

explanation: Always tie bags when they are about 3/4 full. This leaves enough space to close them securely without tearing the plastic. [learn more](GST114_U6_T8#GST114_U6_T8_h4)

question: During Barcode Medication Administration (BCMA), what are the three main things you scan?

options.A: Nurse badge, patient wristband, and medication package
options.B: Dietary tray card, patient chart, and nurse uniform
options.C: Hospital logo, lab tube sticker, and bed frame barcode
options.D: Doctor license, room door number, and IV bag label

explanation: Brilliant! Scanning the nurse, the patient, and the drug is your golden rule to make sure the right meds reach the right person. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the big advantage of using the 'closed gloving' technique in theater?

options.A: It prevents bare hands from touching the outside of the sterile gloves
options.B: It eliminates the need to wear a surgical gown during the case
options.C: It keeps the sterile gloves warmer during long procedures
options.D: It allows the nurse to scrub hands much faster than usual

explanation: By keeping your hands tucked inside your gown sleeves, you can slide your gloves on without your bare skin ever touching the outside surface. [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which condition makes a home birth unsafe because of the high chance of bleeding and delivery complications?

options.A: Mild morning sickness
options.B: Carrying twins
options.C: A history of slight backaches
options.D: Normal weight gain

explanation: Multiple gestations carry a high risk of abnormal positioning and severe bleeding after birth, requiring hospital standby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h4)

question: What three key pieces go into making a complete community health diagnosis?

options.A: The name of the nurse, the hospital budget, and the weather forecast
options.B: The exact number of houses, cars, and electrical poles in the town
options.C: The health problem, the affected population, and the contributing factors
options.D: The list of all available doctors, nurses, and local pharmacists

explanation: Great job! A good diagnosis always states *what* the problem is, *who* is affected, and *why* it is happening in that community. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T1#GNS225_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: To support behind-the-scenes hospital operations and administrative tasks
options.B: To monitor patient vital signs directly at the skin surface
options.C: To replace bedside nurses during surgical procedures
options.D: To diagnose complex diseases without laboratory tests

explanation: Indirect care technologies handle logistics, scheduling, and inventory so that nurses spend less time on paperwork. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is a direct benefit of proper funding at the primary health care level?

options.A: Consistent supply of essential drugs and vaccines
options.B: Construction of multi-story specialist surgical suites
options.C: Automatic promotion of all hospital administrators
options.D: Elimination of all diseases in the country

explanation: Adequate primary care funding directly ensures that basic medications and vaccine cold chains remain stocked and operational. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of incinerating pathological and infectious waste?

options.A: To turn biohazard waste into safe fertilizer for crops
options.B: To recover valuable metals like gold and silver
options.C: To reduce waste volume and destroy pathogens completely
options.D: To generate electricity for the hospital laundry

explanation: High-temperature burning shrinks the physical bulk of the waste while destroying all harmful germs and biological structures. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What does it mean when we say quality improvement tests are 'iterative'?

options.A: They must be performed identically by every hospital in the country
options.B: They are repeated once every ten years by hospital executives
options.C: They involve running multiple small cycles that build upon each other
options.D: They are discarded immediately if the first attempt is imperfect

explanation: Think of 'iterative' as learning as you go. You run a small test, learn from it, and use that lesson to run the next, slightly better cycle! [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is final reporting to the community an essential final step?

options.A: To prove to the government that the nurses deserve a salary raise
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement so nurses can travel abroad
options.C: To advertise private clinics opening in nearby towns
options.D: To maintain transparency and respect for community participation

explanation: Feeding results back to the community shows respect, maintains trust, and encourages continued community-driven health maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: You want villagers to remember proper handwashing steps after an outreach. What is the most practical action to take?

options.A: Distribute illustrated posters showing handwashing steps to take home or place in public areas
options.B: Write the medical names of bacteria on a chalkboard during a one-hour lecture
options.C: Tell the villagers to memorize the steps by repeating them three times in silence
options.D: Ask the village head to verbally test every single resident on handwashing theory

explanation: Pictures speak volumes! Visual posters give people a daily reminder so healthy hygiene habits actually stick. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why is executive leadership commitment critical months after a project has started?

options.A: It allows directors to change the hospital rules every single week
options.B: It guarantees that the hospital will receive international financial grants
options.C: It stops nurses from taking their mandatory annual leave days
options.D: It shows staff that leadership cares about the change beyond the initial launch

explanation: If leaders abandon interest after day one, staff assume the project is just a temporary phase and stop following it. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why can a 'normal' lab result for serum creatinine be misleading when checking a pregnant woman's kidneys?

options.A: Pregnancy causes the liver to produce excess creatinine, confusing lab results
options.B: Laboratory machines are calibrated incorrectly for pregnant patients
options.C: Normal pregnancy lowers creatinine, so a standard reading can mean kidney impairment
options.D: Fetal red blood cells destroy creatinine molecules in the maternal blood

explanation: Because pregnancy naturally speeds up kidney filtration, normal creatinine levels actually drop. So a 'normal' non-pregnant score can actually mean the pregnant kidneys are underperforming! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h4)

question: What do we call a sudden spike in disease cases that goes way above the normal baseline in a region?

options.A: Pandemic
options.B: Epidemic
options.C: Sporadic
options.D: Endemic

explanation: When an illness suddenly surges and hits way more people than usual in an area, that's an epidemic. Great job keeping these terms straight! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h2)

question: Why is taking rifampicin (for TB) alongside certain HIV drugs tricky?

options.A: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in all patients
options.B: Rifampicin alters liver enzymes and can lower antiretroviral blood levels
options.C: Rifampicin stops the absorption of water in the stomach
options.D: The combination immediately destroys the patient's pancreas

explanation: You got it! Rifampicin speeds up liver enzymes so much that it can flush HIV drugs out of the blood too quickly, risking treatment failure. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h6)

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: Where should you place your hands when giving abdominal thrusts to a conscious adult who is choking?

options.A: Across the soft throat area
options.B: Just above the navel
options.C: In the center of the chest
options.D: Directly over the lower ribs

explanation: Correct! Placing your fist just above the belly button (and well below the ribs) lets you push the diaphragm up safely without breaking any bones. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of vocational rehabilitation in mental health CBR?

options.B: To keep clients busy so they do not talk to their family members
